raw_response:
For a community credit union with 400–1,000 members, I would start by evaluating Mifos X. It is the strongest match in this search for a single open-source platform covering savings, loans, transfers and accounting. The other options below address different parts of the job. I have separated evidence available before 15 September 2014 from later or undated material, and I have not tested any of these products with your workload.

1. Mifos X — strongest overall starting point.
[Official June 2014 announcement](https://mifos.org/blog/mifos-initiative-launches-mifos-x-platform-for-financial-inclusion/) identifies an open-source core-banking platform intended for financial institutions, including credit cooperatives. The [public version 1.22.0 changelog](https://github.com/openMF/mifosX-PGS_v2/blob/master/CHANGELOG.md) dates that release to 30 April 2014 and documents fixed and recurring deposits, loan accrual accounting, standing account transfers and loan disbursement into savings. Those features make it a useful candidate for the union's savings, lending and ledger operations. External payment connections and the exact reports your institution requires would still need evaluation; the evidence does not establish that those integrations are already supplied for your location.

2. Cyclos 3.6 — a community payments and account-management alternative.
The [December 2011 release newsletter](https://www.cyclos.org/newsletter/2011_12/) describes GPL software with member accounts, transaction histories, payment authorization, scheduled payments, fees, loans, SMS banking and POS/card interfaces. This is particularly relevant if member payments and a community financial network are central to the requirement. Check the fit of its accounting model and any external bank connections rather than assuming its payment history is a complete general ledger. There is also a material present-day limitation: the [official Cyclos 3 page](https://www.cyclos.org/products/cyclos3/) says it is no longer maintained and discourages mission-critical use. Its relevance to the 2014 question is supported; that does not make the legacy release a suitable current deployment without further work.

3. S.A.F.E. Open Source Microfinance Suite — a broad microfinance suite to inspect.
A [source release dated 3 June 2014](https://sourceforge.net/projects/safemicrofin/files/safe-microfinance/2014.05_152/) establishes pre-cutoff availability. The [later project description](https://sourceforge.net/projects/safemicrofin/) lists loan, cashier, accounting, savings, bank and reporting modules, which together are close to the functions a small credit union needs. The distinction in dates matters: the module list does not prove that every module was already present in the June 2014 build. That build's own notes also identify demanding configuration and only a partial English database translation. I would evaluate a representative loan, deposit and cash transaction before treating it as a practical fit.

4. OpenCBS Desktop — useful lending and savings functions, with later evidence.
The [project page](https://sourceforge.net/projects/opencbs/) describes open-source microfinance core banking with client management, loan schedules, repayments, savings and reporting, plus connections to accounting software, POS terminals and web services. This could supply the member-account and loan side of a solution where accounting or payment processing is separate. The [opened public README](https://github.com/RSKInitiatives/OpenCBS/blob/master/README.md) confirms the client/loan/savings scope, but the release listing I found contains 2016–2017 versions. I therefore cannot establish its availability by the question's September 2014 date from the opened evidence. The current project page also says Desktop is unsupported following its replacement by Cloud in 2019.

5. GnuCash — a ledger component, with a narrower scope.
[GnuCash](https://www.gnucash.org/?lang=en_US) is GPL accounting software, and an [official January 2013 documentation change](https://lists.gnucash.org/pipermail/gnucash-changes/2013-January/011820.html) establishes its double-entry transactions, account registers and multiple ledger splits before the cutoff. It could handle the accounting portion alongside a dedicated member-account system. The opened evidence describes personal and small-business accounting, so I would not present it as a complete credit-union system or assume it supplies multiuser teller operations and payment-network processing.

My practical shortlist would begin with Mifos X, followed by Cyclos if community payments are the dominant need and SAFE if its configuration and language constraints are acceptable. The main unanswered requirement is what “payments” means here: recording deposits and repayments is different from sending money through an external banking network. The searches establish plausible software and components, not a verified production fit for this credit union.
